title: Metals and Non-metals
seo_title: Metals and Non-metals Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Metals and non-metals: properties of metals and non-metals, reactivity series, formation and properties of ionic compounds, basic metallurgical processes, corrosion and its prevention.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3: properties of metals and non-metals, the reactivity series, displacement, ionic compounds, extraction of metals, corrosion and alloys. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one.
key_sub: K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb [H] Cu Hg Ag Au
body_html:
How to think about it

Metals are usually lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors; non-metals are usually dull and brittle. Metals lose electrons to form positive ions; non-metals gain electrons to form negative ions, and the attraction between them makes ionic compounds with high melting points.

The reactivity series lists metals from most to least reactive. A metal displaces any metal below it from a salt solution. Very reactive metals are extracted by electrolysis, metals in the middle by roasting or calcination and then reduction with carbon, and the least reactive by heating alone.

Example

Will copper displace silver from silver nitrate?

copper is above silver

Answer: yes

Example

Electronic configuration of Mg (Z = 12)?

2 in K, 8 in L, 2 in M

Answer: 2, 8, 2

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a less reactive metal can displace a more reactive one.
  • Saying ionic compounds conduct electricity as solids.
  • Mixing up roasting (sulphide ores) and calcination (carbonate ores).

faq.q: Why are ionic compounds hard with high melting points?
faq.a: Strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions hold them in a rigid lattice.

faq.q: How can corrosion of iron be prevented?
faq.a: By painting, oiling, greasing, galvanising, chrome plating, anodising or making alloys such as stainless steel.

items.q: How is zinc obtained from zinc blende (ZnS)?
c: roasting to ZnO, then reduction with carbon
items.e: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂; ZnO + C → Zn + CO.

items.q: How is copper purified?
c: electrolytic refining with impure copper as the anode
items.e: Pure copper collects on the cathode.

items.q: What is the property of metals that lets them be drawn into wires?
items.e: Malleability means they can be beaten into sheets.

items.q: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
items.e: Copper is next and is cheaper, so it is used in wires.

items.q: Why is sodium kept under kerosene?
c: it reacts strongly with air and water and can catch fire
items.e: Potassium is also kept in kerosene.

items.q: What is an amphoteric oxide?
c: an oxide that reacts with both acids and bases, such as Al₂O₃ and ZnO
an oxide that reacts with neither
items.e: Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O.

items.q: Why does calcium float when added to water?
c: bubbles of hydrogen stick to its surface
items.e: Magnesium floats in hot water for the same reason.

items.q: What is brass made of?

items.q: What is aqua regia?

items.e: It means 'royal water'.

items.q: Which metals are the poorest conductors of heat?
items.e: Most metals conduct heat well.

items.q: How are highly reactive metals such as sodium obtained?
c: by electrolytic reduction of their molten chlorides
items.e: Carbon cannot reduce them.

items.q: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity?
c: when molten or dissolved in water
items.e: The ions can then move.

items.q: What is gangue?

items.e: It is removed before extraction.

items.q: Which non-metal is lustrous?
items.e: Iodine crystals are shiny.

items.q: Which metal is used in the thermit reaction to join railway tracks?

items.q: What is solder made of, and why is it used for welding wires?

lead and tin; it has a low melting point
copper and zinc; it is magnetic
items.e: Alloys often melt lower than their metals.

pure gold is too soft, so it is alloyed with silver or copper
items.e: 22-carat gold is 22 parts gold in 24.

items.q: What is roasting?
c: heating a sulphide ore strongly in excess air
heating a carbonate ore in limited air
items.e: This turns the sulphide into an oxide.

items.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?

items.q: What is an alloy?

a compound of a metal and oxygen
items.e: Brass, bronze and steel are alloys.
